arxiv-2008-09261.title: Dynamic change of gene-to-gene regulatory networks in response to SARS-CoV-2 infection
arxiv-2008-09261.creator: Yoshihisa Tanaka, Kako Higashihara, Mai Adachi Nakazawa, Fumiyoshi Yamashita, Yoshinori Tamada, Yasushi Okuno
arxiv-2008-09261.description: Abstract Abstract The current pandemic of SARS-CoV-2 has caused extensive damage to society. The characterization of SARS-CoV-2 prpfiles has been addressed by researchers globally with the aim of resolving this disruptive crisis. This investigation process is indispensable for an understanding of how SARS-CoV-2 behaves in human host cells.

arxiv-2103-09357.title: A new practical framework for the stability analysis of perturbed saddle-point problems and applications Thanks: J. Kraus and M. Lymbery acknowledge the support of this work by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) as part of the project “Physics-oriented solvers for
arxiv-2103-09357.creator: Qingguo Hong*, Johannes Kraus, Maria Lymbery, Fadi Philo
arxiv-2103-09357.description: Abstract . In this paper we prove a new abstract stability result for perturbed saddle-point problems based on a norm fitting technique. We derive the stability condition according to Babuška’s theory from a small inf-sup condition, similar to the famous Ladyzhenskaya-Babuška-Brezzi (LBB) condition, and the other standard assumptions in Brezzi’s theory, in a combined abstract norm.

arxiv-2108-01642.title: Separating topological recurrence from measurable recurrence: exposition and extension of Kriz’s example
arxiv-2108-01642.creator: John T. Griesmer
arxiv-2108-01642.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by John T. Griesmer. We prove that for every infinite set E ⊆ ℤ E\subseteq\mathbb{Z} , there is a set S ⊆ E − E S\subseteq E-E which is a set of topological recurrence and not a set of measurable recurrence. This extends a result of Igor Kriz, proving that there is a set of topological recurrence which is not a set of measurable recurrence. Our construction follows Kriz’s closely, and this paper can be considered an exposition of the original argument.

arxiv-2109-03814.title: Panoptic SegFormer: Delving Deeper into Panoptic Segmentation with Transformers
arxiv-2109-03814.creator: Zhiqi Li, Wenhai Wang, Enze Xie, Zhiding Yu, Anima Anandkumar, Jose M. Alvarez, Ping Luo, Tong Lu, [0.15cm] Nanjing University Shanghai AI Laboratory The University of Hong Kong NVIDIA Caltech[0.15cm] lzq@smail.nju.edu.cn wangwenhai@pjlab.org.cn xieenze@hku.hk zhidingy@nvidia.com aanandkumar@nvidia.
arxiv-2109-03814.description: Abstract Panoptic segmentation involves a combination of joint semantic segmentation and instance segmentation, where image contents are divided into two types: things and stuff. We present Panoptic SegFormer, a general framework for panoptic segmentation with transformers. It contains three innovative components: an efficient deeply-supervised mask decoder, a query decoupling strategy, and an improved post-processing method.

arxiv-2202-03681.title: Breakdown of Linear Spin-wave Theory and Existence of Spinon Bound States in the Frustrated Kagome Lattice Antiferromagnet
arxiv-2202-03681.creator: K. Matan, T. Ono, S. Ohira-Kawamura, K. Nakajima, Y. Nambu, T. J. Sato
arxiv-2202-03681.description: Abstract Spin dynamics of the spin-1/2 kagome lattice antiferromagnet Cs 2 Cu 3 SnF 12 was studied using high-resolution, time-of-flight inelastic neutron scattering. The flat mode, a characteristic of the frustrated kagome antiferromagnet, and the low-energy dispersive mode, which is dominated by magnons, can be well described by the linear spin-wave theory.

arxiv-2207-14334.title: ThielSort: Implementing the Diverting Fast Radix Algorithm DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: ACM Journal of Experimental Algorithmics; Feb. 20, 2022; Woodstock, NY Price: 15.00 ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 CCS: Theory of computation Sorting and searching CCS: Theory of computation Divide and conquer
arxiv-2207-14334.creator: Stuart Thiel, Larry Thiel, Gregory Butler
arxiv-2207-14334.description: Abstract . This paper presents ThielSort, a practical implementation of the Diverting Fast Radix (DFR) Algorithm. The theoretical improvements over classical radix sorts are outlined and implementation details are specified to demonstrate that the algorithm is competitive with the state of the art.

arxiv-2212-10329.title: Spectral and Combinatorial Aspects of Cayley-Crystals Thanks: This work was supported by the U.S. National Science Foundation through the grants DMR-1823800 and CMMI-2131760.
arxiv-2212-10329.creator: Fabian R. Lux, Emil Prodan
arxiv-2212-10329.description: Abstract . Owing to their interesting spectral properties, the synthetic crystals over lattices other than regular Euclidean lattices, such as hyperbolic and fractal ones, have attracted renewed attention, especially from materials and meta-materials research communities. They can be studied under the umbrella of quantum dynamics over Cayley graphs of finitely generated groups.

arxiv-2302-14518.title: Generalization Error Bounds for Noisy, Iterative Algorithms via Maximal Leakage
arxiv-2302-14518.creator: Ibrahim Issa, Amedeo Roberto Esposito, Michael Gastpar
arxiv-2302-14518.description: Abstract We adopt an information-theoretic framework to analyze the generalization behavior of the class of iterative, noisy learning algorithms. This class is particularly suitable for study under information-theoretic metrics as the algorithms are inherently randomized, and it includes commonly used algorithms such as Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics (SGLD).

arxiv-2304-03862.title: NOMA-aided double RIS under Nakagami- m m fading: Channel and System Modelling
arxiv-2304-03862.creator: Wilson de Souza Junior, Taufik Abrão
arxiv-2304-03862.description: Abstract We investigate the downlink outage performance of double-RIS-aided non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), where a near-BS and a near-users RISs setup are deployed. To extend the coverage to 360 degrees, we deploy a simultaneously transmitting and reflecting RIS (STAR-RIS) structure aiming to improve communication reliability for both indoor and outdoor users.

arxiv-2401-10330.title: Optimal sampling of tensor networks targeting wave function’s fast decaying tails
arxiv-2401-10330.creator: Marco Ballarin, Pietro Silvi, Simone Montangero, Daniel Jaschke
arxiv-2401-10330.description: Abstract We introduce an optimal strategy to sample quantum outcomes of local measurement strings for isometric tensor network states. Our method generates samples based on an exact cumulative bounding function, without prior knowledge, in the minimal amount of tensor network contractions. The algorithm avoids sample repetition and, thus, is efficient at sampling distribution with exponentially decaying tails.

arxiv-2406-12911.title: The Promise of Analog Deep Learning: Recent Advances, Challenges and Opportunities
arxiv-2406-12911.creator: ADITYA DATAR* 1, PRAMIT SAHA* 2
arxiv-2406-12911.description: Abstract Much of the present-day Artificial Intelligence (AI) utilizes artificial neural networks, which are sophisticated computational models designed to recognize patterns and solve complex problems by learning from data. However, a major bottleneck occurs during a device’s calculation of weighted sums for forward propagation and optimization procedure for backpropagation, especially for deep neural networks, or networks with numerous layers.

arxiv-2505-08297.title: Capacity of Entanglement in Lifshitz Theories
arxiv-2505-08297.description: Abstract We study the capacity of entanglement in certain integrable scale invariant theories that exhibit Lifshitz scaling symmetry with a generic dynamical exponent z z at the critical point. This measure characterizes the width of the eigenvalue spectrum of the reduced density matrix and is a quantum informational counterpart of heat capacity.

arxiv-2507-20882.title: Electroweak corrections to Higgs+jet production in gluon fusion
arxiv-2507-20882.creator: Long-Bin Chen, Hai Tao Li, and Wen-Long Sang
arxiv-2507-20882.description: Abstract We present the calculation of complete next-to-leading order electroweak corrections to the Higgs boson production in g ​ g → g ​ H gg\to gH channel. We apply the method of differential equations combined with the selection of optimized master integrals to accomplish the calculation of master integrals. We consider three distinct α \alpha schemes.

arxiv-2511-15582.title: Stability bounds for the generalized Kadanoff-Baym ansatz in the Holstein dimer
arxiv-2511-15582.creator: O. Moreno Segura, Y. Pavlyukh, R. Tuovinen
arxiv-2511-15582.description: Abstract Predicting real‐time dynamics in correlated systems is demanding: exact two‐time Green’s function methods are accurate but often too costly, while the Generalized Kadanoff-Baym Ansatz (GKBA) offers time-linear propagation at the risk of uncontrolled behavior. We examine when and why GKBA fails in a minimal yet informative setting, the Holstein dimer that describes electron-phonon coupling.

pmc-10665957.creator: Guangdong Liu, Cui Yang, Xin Wang, Xi Chen, Yanjiang Wang, Weidong Le
pmc-10665957.description: Oxygen metabolism abnormality plays a crucial role in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) via several mechanisms, including hypoxia, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Hypoxia condition usually results from living in a high-altitude habitat, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, and chronic obstructive sleep apnea.

pmc-10671220.description: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a metabolic disease characterized by chronic hyperglycemia associated with impaired carbohydrate, lipid, and protein metabolism, with concomitant absence of insulin secretion or reduced sensitivity to its metabolic effects. Patients with diabetes mellitus have a 30% more risk of developing heart failure and cardiovascular disease compared to healthy people.

pmc-11318898.creator: Nawal Hamdan Almohammadi
pmc-11318898.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundPathology laboratory classes are traditionally conducted using a conventional light microscope. The Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic and recent technological advances necessitated remote learning through online classes using virtual slides (VS) instead of glass slides (GS).AimThe purpose of this study was to gauge the perception of learning pathology using virtual slides (VS) as opposed to glass slides (GS) for medical students in Saudi Arabia.

pmc-11429154.title: Transfer learning-enabled outcome prediction for guiding CRRT treatment of the pediatric patients with sepsis
pmc-11429154.creator: Xiao-Qing Li, Rui-Quan Wang, Lian-Qiang Wu, Dong-Mei Chen
pmc-11429154.description: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is a life-saving procedure for sepsis but the benefit of CRRT varies and prediction of clinical outcomes is valuable in efficient treatment planning. This study aimed to use machine learning (ML) models trained using MIMIC III data for identifying sepsis patients who would benefit from CRRT.

pmc-13272266.creator: Kateřina Klíčová, Kateřina Menšíková, Dorota Šebelová, Petra Polčáková, Michal Kaleta, Sarah Elizabeth Victoria Cook, Zuzana Ildžová, Lenka Satke, Dalibor Zimek, Petr Kaňovský
